prize_parts.citation: For turning targeted protein degradation into a designable chemical principle, by using small molecules to bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together: the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target through which thalidomide-class molecular glues act

statement.case_for: I have changed my preferred configuration from B014 to B036. The deciding point is what each case can show to a physicist's standard. For degraders the principle is simple (a small molecule forces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, and the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery does the work), the mechanism has been checked directly (crystal structures of VHL and cereblon ternary complexes explain selectivity and cooperativity), and it has been reproduced by very many laboratories. It also opens a capability that did not exist: targets with no druggable pocket can be removed rather than inhibited, and the thalidomide-class drugs, empirically discovered, now have a molecular explanation. The discovery can be separated from later refinement: Crews and Deshaies conceived the heterobifunctional degrader, and Handa identified cereblon as the direct target of thalidomide, which is the anchor for the glue half. Four colleagues independently reached this from different fields, and I have tested that convergence against the evidence rather than counted it. My round-1 timing objection (no approved PROTAC) was answered by Zou and Chabes: a prize recognises a discovery whose mechanism is established, not a regulatory milestone, and the citation can be written to say so. The citation is stated as a principle, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, covering both the designed and the discovered versions of it.
statement.case_against: The three-person limit excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and the trio joins two discoveries that were made at different times by different groups, so the citation must be careful not to imply a single event. No PROTAC is approved, so impact is partly prospective. Against B014, which I still regard as scientifically attractive: the in vivo condensate debate is real, the chemistry-versus-cell-biology question is unresolved for several members, Pappu and Mittag are excluded, and in this discussion only Sparr and I held it first, so it has not shown a route to five without changing the citation to a narrower claim.

responses.point: Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are enabling refinement, and Handa, not Ciulli, is the originating discovery for glues; Zou would accept Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as second best.
responses.response: I now agree with you and Chabes on the criterion I asked the committee to apply in round 1: separate the original discovery from the refinement. Cereblon as the thalidomide target is a discovery about nature; VHL ligands made PROTACs drug-like and the crystal structures explained them, which is important but follows from the principle. I accept your point that the glue half then rests on one person while the PROTAC half has two, and the citation should say so honestly by naming the two lines under one principle. I would not move to Ciulli, but I would want the report to credit his structures explicitly.

responses.point: The citation should centre on induced proximity to an E3 ligase, covering bifunctional PROTACs and thalidomide-class glues, and be stated as a principle and not a drug modality.
responses.response: This is what moved me. In round 1 I said the ranking showed popularity and not settled attribution; on reflection the attribution of the three anchors (PROTAC concept by Crews and Deshaies, cereblon by Handa) is no less defensible than my own B014 trio, and your point that the mechanism is reproduced independently counts for more than my worry about approval. I accept your wording that names cereblon explicitly, since it prevents the citation from reading as a pipeline claim.

responses.point: A Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio covers the PROTAC concept and the molecular glue mechanism in one coherent citation, with no PROTAC yet approved being a timing concern and not a barrier.
responses.response: I disagreed in round 1 that two achievements were joined under one citation. I now think they are one principle seen from two sides, designed bifunctionality and discovered monovalent glues acting through the same ligase-recruitment logic, provided the citation states the principle and names both routes. The residual risk you also acknowledge, that the prize could be read as an endorsement of a clinical pipeline, is manageable through the wording and I will press for that in the vote.

responses.point: B014 should name a physical-chemical principle without claiming every condensate is a liquid, and credit may need to lean to the molecular framework (Rosen, Pappu, Mittag) more than the founding observation.
responses.response: We share the view that a B014 citation must rest on multivalency and phase behaviour in reconstituted systems and avoid the in vivo claim, and I still think that citation is scientifically defensible. But your point shows the cost: the more we lean toward the molecular framework, the more Pappu and Mittag displace Hyman or Brangwynne, and the founding observation that makes the idea recognisable is no longer in the citation. I cannot find a three-name configuration that is both faithful to history and chemical enough for five votes, so I rank it second and keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: B034 is a fully mature, daily-use method with clean two-person attribution, and Kosugi should not be credited.
responses.response: I agree with your reading of Kosugi: stoichiometric tin amide chemistry is an antecedent, not a laureate contribution, and I would not add him. My hesitation, shared by Zou and Aqvist, is that after the 2010 cross-coupling prize this is a refinement of an honoured paradigm and the committee would have to explain why now. I regard it as a credible mature alternative, but I did not rank it above B036 on generative potential, and I keep B023 as my second alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee wants the citation to be a single principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) or separate PROTAC and glue parts; I propose one principle and would not split it.
Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I choose Handa as the originating discovery for glues but the Ciulli case is not frivolous.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC will weigh with colleagues more than I now think it should.
Whether I am discounting B014 fairly: the in vivo condensate issue may be a problem of interpretation and not of the core principle, and a future prize could be warranted once that settles.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no collaboration, funding or institutional tie to any credited name on any shortlisted candidate. Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr are Lund colleagues, and none of us has a tie to a candidate, so no recusal applies. My own switch away from B014 is based on the scientific case, not on any relationship.
